abstract: Turgor pressure, which drives irreversible cell wall enlargement and thereby cell growth, is isotropic. Polarized plant cell growth therefore requires spatially regulated wall-loosening to confine growth to specific domains. These domains are often marked by localized ROP GTPase activity, but how this polarity is translated into localized wall loosening remains unclear. Here, we investigated the delivery of EXPA7, a trichoblast-specific -expansin that facilitates wall loosening and enlargement during root hair growth. We show that ROP activation directs EXPA7 recruitment to the root hair initiation domain through brefeldin-A-sensitive vesicular trafficking, with YIP4a/b required for its normal secretion and wall-deposition. The recruited EXPA7 contributes to ROP2-induced wall enlargement, and its accumulation accompanies local cell wall bulging. Our findings provide a mechanistic link between ROP activation and cell growth, suggesting how signals converging on ROP activation may control growth.
